newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Liberian warlord Kromah apologises over arms cache.
newsitem.headline: Liberian warlord Kromah apologises over arms cache.

text.p: Liberian warlord and presidential hopeful Alhaji Kromah on Friday apologised for keeping an illegal arms cache at his home but said he had planned to hand it over to peacekeepers all along.

Kromah, who was arrested on March 7 and placed under house arrest after discovery of the arms, said he had not intended to use the arms and reiterated his support for the West African sponsored peace deal to end seven years of civil war.
"I wish to admit the error of having arms at my residence after the January deadline for disarmament," he told a news conference in a statement.
"The arms were never intended for any evil motives, rather they were intended for delivery to (the West African peacekeeping force) ECOMOG," he said.
"There was no plan and will never be a plan by me or any of my associates to engage in any activities, military or otherwise, to undermine this peace process for which we have worked so hard."

Kromah, who hopes to contest the May 30 presidential election, was accompanied by the chief of staff of the Nigerian-led peacekeeping force, Brigadier Abdoul One-Mohammed, and Liberia's justice minister, Peter Bonnor Jallah.
Kromah gave the news conference, his first public reaction to the affair, at his seaside residence in eastern Monrovia. He remains under house arrest with ECOMOG tanks and troops on patrol there.
"I do not feel too big to apologise for the error and wish to assure you of my determination to help ensure the successful completion of the peace process," he said.
West African leaders brokered the peace deal, which followed a dozen failed accords, in Nigeria's capital Abuja last August. It envisaged disarmament followed by May elections.
ECOMOG commander General Victor Malu expressed confidence after the disarmament process ended early in February that national elections could go ahead as planned.
Freed American slaves set up Liberia in 1847 and their descendents dominated the West African nation until a 1980 coup by the indigenous krahn ethnic group.
Rival faction leaders Charles Taylor, who launched the war in December 1989, and George Boley, representing the krahn, have also announced their intention to run for president.
Well over 150,000 people have been killed by the war.
